critical_logical_distinction.certificate_farkas_test: Fix the actual CAG sigma and a truly optimal pi. Any rational f satisfying every graph arc and d.f < n*min_b sum_a pi_a*f_(b+ea,a) separates all normalized independent Q and nonnegative lambda. f need not itself be CAG. To separate the potential-projected certificate, f must also equal Phi(q)-Phi(q-ea) on every n and n-1 coordinate, which the 84-point tables do.
critical_logical_distinction.existential_optimum: H_root needs some optimal pi. A separator for one nonunique optimizer is insufficient unless all optimal pi are excluded. The 34-customer optimum is unique, so its exact pi is the right test.
critical_logical_distinction.positive_comparison_meaning: The positive pi34 gaps below mean these particular saved potential witnesses do not separate H_root for customer34. They neither provide lambda,Q nor prove feasibility.
critical_logical_distinction.unscaled_arc_convention: F_(q,a)>=F_(r,a) iff r_a>=q_a and r_b<=q_b for b!=a, with |q|=|r|=n. This report checks every such nonself comparison; no scaled hyperarc is silently treated as an incidence edge.
critical_logical_distinction.purequery_vs_mixedquery: For deterministic a, Q independence from query is vacuous. Combining certificates Q^(a) for different pure queries yields correlated mass pi_a Q_b^(a). It is generally not the required product pi_a Q_b. Pure-query certificates cannot be averaged into H_root without a common Q.
